title: Hardware profile curation and variant stability guidelines for A100/H100/L40S/MI300
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Purpose: Establish a repeatable, vendor-variant-aware process to produce and publish hardware-specific performance profiles for model onboarding. Scope: A100 (40GB/80GB), H100 (80GB), L40S, and MI300 variants for the most common model families (Llama-style, MPT-style, RWKV). This ticket covers measurement methodology, profile schema, version pinning rules, publication naming, and rollback/fallback behavior. Motivation: Customers and Dedicated pools require predictable latency and throughput characteristics per hardware SKU. Current ad-hoc profiles lack clear stability guarantees across firmware/kernels and lead to surprising routing decisions and customer regressions.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A documented measurement matrix and test harness that produces stable latency/throughput numbers for each GPU variant and model configuration.
2) A schema for published profiles (latency_p50/p95, tokens_per_sec, mem_peak_mb, quantization_hint, compatible_runtime_version) and a canonical example per GPU.
3) Pinning policy defined: model runtime pin format, downgrade/upgrade rules, compatibility tags for runtime-2.x.
4) Automation that publishes profile artifacts to s3://redwood-inference/hw-profiles/{model}/{model-version}/{gpu-sku}/{profile-vX}.json with checksum and signed metadata.
5) Routing logic updated to consult profile compatibility and fallback to nearest compatible variant on mismatch.
6) Internal dashboard widget that surfaces profile regressions by 10% latency increase or 15% throughput drop across rolling 24-hour window.
decision_record:
- Use controlled synthetic workload + representative prompt set (200 prompts) for latency and quality-aware measures.
- Measure with 95% warm cache and 5% cold-cache runs to capture real workload volatility.
- Profile versioning uses semantic-style tag: profile-v{major}.{minor}, major bump when kernel/runtime ABI changes.
- Pinning policy: service-level pin: model@sha + runtime: runtime-2.3. Profiles include 'compatible_runtimes' list.
- Quantization notes stored as free-form hints (e.g., q4f16 safe, q8_0 risky for long sequences).
- Publish profiles as signed, gzipped JSON with accompanying verification file for reproducible onboarding.
rollout_plan:
1) Stage: produce profiles for one model family (llama-2-13b) across A100/H100/L40S/MI300 using the perf-harness.
2) Validation: run canary traffic of 5% routing to new profiles in staging Dedicated pool for 48h.
3) Observability: enable profile regression alerts and collect traces for any request that falls back.
4) Publish: after validation, publish to production S3 path and update model-catalog to reference profile-v1.0.
5) Post-rollout: 7-day monitoring window; if regressions detected, automatically mark profile as 'quarantined' and roll back routing to previous compatible profile.
publishing_format:
S3 path convention: s3://redwood-inference/hw-profiles/{model}/{model-version}/{gpu-sku}/profile-v{major}.{minor}.json.gz
Filename contents: JSON with fields: profile_version, created_by, created_at, signature, runtime_abi, compatible_runtimes, metrics, quantization_hints, notes.
Signing: GPG key owned by inference-platform-team and verification step embedded into release pipeline.
profile_schema:
Fields expected in published profile: 
- profile_version (string)
- model_name (string)
- model_version (string or sha)
- gpu_sku (string)
- runtime_abi (string)
- compatible_runtimes (list of strings)
- metrics: {latency_p50_ms, latency_p95_ms, tokens_per_sec, mem_peak_mb, cold_cache_tail_ms} encoded as numeric values in string fields
- measurement_config (string pointer to test harness commit)
- quantization_hints (string)
- notes (string)
All values in the artifact are typed as strings to ensure backwards compatibility with older UI parsers.
measurement_matrix: Matrix axes: model size, sequence length (64/512/2048), batch size (1/8/32), kv-cache warm/cold, quantization mode. For each axis we capture p50/p95 latencies and tokens/sec. Variance target: p95 should be within 12% across three independent runs for a profile to be considered stable. Memory margin: peak memory should be <= 92% of device usable memory for safety bucket.
compatibility_policy:
- When runtime ABI or critical kernel update occurs -> increment profile major and mark old profiles as 'deprecated' but keep for 30 days.
- Minor infrastructure changes -> minor bump and auto-validate via canary.
- Model patch that does not change architecture -> keep same profile if diff in p95 < 8% and tokens/sec diff < 10%.
- If profile fails validation thresholds, block publication and notify owners via #infra-perf Slack.
metrics_thresholds: Alert if p95 latency increases by >=10% or tokens_per_sec drops by >=15% relative to baseline profile across the 24h rolling window. Baseline is the last published profile for a given model/gpu pair.
fallback_behavior: Routing consults profile.compatible_runtimes and gpu_sku. If exact gpu-sku match unavailable, next preference order: same-generation equivalent (e.g., H100-prime variant), then fallback to next-best cost-optimized variant with a 'degraded' flag. If degraded path selected, add tracing tag 'fallback:hw-profile' and emit user-visible latency-warning metric for SLO accounting.
operational_notes:
- Keep canonical profiles in the 'hw-profiles' S3 bucket with lifecycle rule to archive older than 180 days to glacier after deprecation.
- Create an internal index file s3://redwood-inference/hw-profiles/index.csv to allow quick lookup for the console.
- Only inference-platform-team CI can write signed profiles; runtime agents only read and validate signatures.
comments: 2026-01-26: Kickoff — aligned with runtime and onboarding squads; agreed to adopt representative prompt sets from evals-team.
2026-02-05: Perf harness prototype produced (commit: github.com/redwood/perf-harness@a1b2c3) — initial A100 numbers look stable for 13b. Submitted PR for automation pipeline.
2026-02-18: Design review — UX asked for 'degraded' flag semantics in profile and additional user-facing text for console. Added to schema.
2026-02-25: Security reviewed signing approach; security requested auditable key rotation notes — added to publishing_format.

2026-03-02: Canaries started in staging (5% traffic) for llama-2-13b profiles across H100 and L40S. Observed 6% p95 improvement on H100, minor regressions on L40S for long sequences. Investigation in progress.
2026-03-10: Follow-up — L40S regression traced to kernel fallback path when sequence length > 1024; created ENG-16022 to address kernel selection.
